A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet. Everything you send goes through it scrambled, so nobody in between can read it.

Here is how it works:

Your device locks (encrypts) your traffic before it leaves.
The locked traffic travels to the VPN company's computer.
That computer unlocks it and sends it on to the website you wanted.
The website sees the VPN's address, not yours, so it looks like you are browsing from there.

This helps on public Wi-Fi, because strangers on the same network can't read your traffic. It also hides your location from websites. It does not make you fully anonymous, since the VPN company can still see where you go, so pick one you trust.
